chunks: And in the hadith of Yazeed ibn Is'haq from Abu Sadiq, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) exhorting the people in three places: Al-Jamal, Siffeen, and the day of Al-Nahr.

He would say: O servants of Allah, fear Allah, lower your gazes, lower your voices, reduce your speech, and accustom yourselves to confrontation, debate, dueling, struggling, grappling, and advancing; then stand firm and remember Allah much, perhaps you may succeed.
And do not dispute among yourselves lest you become weary and your strength depart, and be patient, for indeed Allah is with the patient.
ai.seo_question: What were the key ethical and military instructions given by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) during the major battles?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (as) strategic emphasis on psychological and physical discipline during the three pivotal conflicts of his caliphate: Al-Jamal, Siffeen, and Nahrawan. By instructing the troops to lower their gazes and voices, he sought to minimize distractions and internal friction, ensuring that their focus remained on steadfastness (thabat) and divine remembrance amidst the chaos of battle. This advice underscores the Shia scholarly view that spiritual composure is as critical as martial prowess in achieving victory.

en.hubeali:
And in a Hadeeth of Yazeed Bin Is’haq, from Abu Sadiq who said, 
‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> calling the people in three places – The (battles of the) Camel, and Siffeen and the day of Al-Nahr (Battle of Naharwaan), saying: ‘

Servants of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and lower your eyes, and minimise your voices, and lessen your speeches, and resign yourselves upon the confrontation, and the arguments, and the duelling, and the struggling, and the clasping, and the advancing; and mention Allah<sup>azwj</sup> a lot so that you may be successful,
and do not dispute for you would become weary and your strength would depart, and be patient for [2:153] surely Allah is with the patient’.
en.sarwar: 2. In the Hadith of ibn Ishaq the following is narrated from abu Sadiq who has said the following: “I heard Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, encourage people during three battle places. They were the battle of al- Jamal, Siffin and al-Nahrawan.

He spoke to people and said, ‘Servants of Allah, you must maintain piety before Allah and cast down your eyes, lower your voices, reduce your speeches, settle your soul on walking in the arena of war to do your best. Face the enemy, make best use of your weapons, strive to win, close up on to the enemy, force your enemy to flee and stay steadfast. Speak of Allah very often, perhaps you succeed.
You must not quarrel among yourselves lest you fail and will be humiliated. Exercise patience; Allah is with those who exercise patience.’”
